Maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a sampling profile on prompt caching and found really low canonical key hit rates for short system prompts.
Maria: baseline expected hit rate ~60% for tiny prompts (<40 tokens), actual observed 18%.
Ajay: Oof. Any examples of mismatched keys? normalization issues?
Maria: Yep. Most hits are missed because clients send slightly different spacing, stray trailing punctuation, and client-side snippet ids. Example keys:
Maria: 'sys:Welcome' vs 'sys: Welcome ' -> different keys.
Kevin: Also seeing kernel selection churn on those requests — small prompts fall back to the generic kernel which triggers an immediate KV flush on first token, killing warmup.
Olivia: Interesting. Is this visible at API level or only internal runtime traces?
Maria: Both. API logs show duplicate cache-miss writes; runtime trace shows kernel switch timestamp aligned with cache write.
Ajay: Can we canonicalize keys at the edge (gateway) before routing? We could normalize whitespace, strip trailing punctuation, and map known snippet ids to stable ids.
Maria: Proposed header for opt-in canonicalization: `x-rw-cache-opt: canonicalize=v1`.
Maria: Quick curl example:
Maria: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'x-rw-cache-opt: canonicalize=v1' -H 'x-rw-cache-scope: conversation' -d '{"prompt":"Hello, world"}'
```
Kevin: One catch: streaming clients sometimes retry with the header stripped when they resume. That produces duplicate warmups and confuses batching heuristics.
Olivia: Could we enforce canonicalization server-side even if client doesn't opt-in? Backcompat concerns?
Ajay: We can run canonicalization by default but gate strict mapping behind the header. Default = lightweight normalize (trim/normalize whitespace). Strict = id mapping + punctuation normalization.
perf-bot: perf-alert: tail latency +12% for short prompt cohort since canary 2027-08-01 (matched to kernel fallback events)
Maria: Triage notes: 1) Add gateway lightweight canonicalization (safe) 2) Add canonicalize=v1 header for strict mapping 3) Instrument client SDKs to preserve header on retries/stream resumes 4) Update batching heuristic to prefer stable-kernel grouping for first N tokens.
Kevin: Also need to adjust kernel selection: if request has `x-rw-cache-opt` set, force the cached-path kernel to avoid KV flush on first token.
Olivia: I'll open a small RFC + SDK patch. Also need an integration test for stream-resume preserving headers.
Ajay: For rollout: Canary gateway with lightweight canonicalize on 10% traffic + SDK patch, measure hit-rate and p95. Target: hit-rate >50% and tail latency drop < -8%.
Maria: Adding logs for 'cache_key_original' and 'cache_key_canonical' for 7 days to analyze.
Kevin: Ping me when the canary is up, I'll add runtime perf counters for kernel-switch events.
Olivia: I'll coordinate with SDK team — will send PR link shortly.
perf-bot: note: alert cleared in canary env after manual flag 'force_cached_kernel=true' applied.
Maria: Thanks all — will collate into a postmortem-style doc after canary results.
